subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Christianity Beliefs Marriage The Family Living The Christian Life Matters Of Life Death Spec A
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the term 'sanctity of life' mean?
options: That only human achievement matters
That life has no special value
That life is sacred and God-given, and should be respected
That life is purely a matter of chance
questions.explain: Sanctity of life is the belief that life is holy, God-given and deserving of special respect.

questions.q: Which statement reflects a view supporting gender equality found in many modern religious communities?
options: Women should never take part in worship
Gender roles can never change
Only men can possess a soul
Men and women have equal value and dignity before God
questions.explain: Many believers hold that, while roles may differ, men and women are of equal worth and dignity.

questions.q: What is a common misconception about religious views on same-sex relationships?
options: That a range of views exists across and within faiths
That denominations can differ on this issue
That some accept and some reject such relationships
That all religious people hold exactly the same view
questions.explain: The misconception is believing all religious people hold exactly the same view; in reality attitudes to same-sex relationships vary widely both within and between religions.

questions.q: Which of the following is commonly described as a purpose of the family in religious teaching?
options: To avoid all responsibility for others
To replace the need for community
To isolate members from wider society
To bring up children and pass on faith and values
questions.explain: Many faiths see the family as the place where children are nurtured and religious and moral values are passed on.

questions.q: Which is a reason some couples give for choosing to cohabit rather than marry?
options: They want to test their compatibility before any lifelong commitment
Cohabitation is required by religious law
Marriage is illegal in the UK
Cohabitation guarantees children
questions.explain: Some couples cohabit to test their relationship or because they do not see marriage as necessary, though some faiths discourage this.

questions.q: What does the Christian idea of 'dominion' over creation traditionally mean?
options: Humans may destroy nature freely
Humans must never use natural resources
Nature has authority over humans
Humans are given responsibility and authority to care for creation
questions.explain: Dominion is often interpreted as responsible authority and care, not the right to exploit.

questions.q: Which statement reflects a secular (non-religious) view of marriage often held in the UK today?
options: Marriage must always be arranged
Only religious people may marry
Marriage is one valid option, and cohabitation or civil partnership are equally acceptable
Marriage is forbidden by law
questions.explain: Many non-religious people see marriage as one of several equally valid ways to form a committed relationship.

questions.q: What is 'IVF' an example of?
options: An environmental policy
A fertility treatment helping couples conceive
A form of capital punishment
A type of euthanasia
questions.explain: IVF (in-vitro fertilisation) is a fertility treatment that helps couples who struggle to conceive.

questions.q: What is the difference between active and passive euthanasia?
options: Active involves doing something to end life; passive involves withdrawing or withholding treatment
Passive euthanasia is a form of fertility treatment
Active is always legal and passive is always illegal
They mean exactly the same thing
questions.explain: Active euthanasia means taking direct action to end life, while passive euthanasia means allowing death by stopping treatment.

questions.q: Which statement best reflects the view of Christians who fully support women being ordained as priests or ministers?
options: Only men were created in God's image
Women cannot serve God in any role
Leadership should be based on calling and gifts, not gender
Worship should exclude women entirely
questions.explain: Many Christians argue that women and men are equally called to leadership, based on gifts rather than gender.

questions.q: Why do some Christians believe procreation is an important purpose of sex?
options: Because it removes the need for marriage
Because the law requires every couple to have children
Because the Bible includes the command to 'be fruitful and multiply'
Because it is the only purpose sex can have
questions.explain: The Genesis command to 'be fruitful and multiply' is often cited to support procreation as a purpose of sex.

questions.q: What is 'polygamy'?
options: Choosing lifelong celibacy
Being married to more than one person at the same time
Marrying within the same family
Living together without marriage
questions.explain: Polygamy is the practice of having more than one spouse at the same time, accepted in some cultures but not in UK law.

questions.q: Why might a religious believer object to using animals in cosmetic testing?
options: Because animals have no place in creation
Because animals cannot feel anything
Because causing unnecessary suffering conflicts with the duty to treat creation with care
Because cosmetics are forbidden
questions.explain: Many believers oppose testing that causes needless animal suffering, as stewardship calls for kindness to creation.

questions.q: What is 'euthanasia'?
options: The painless ending of a life to relieve suffering
A funeral ceremony
A medical examination
A type of fertility treatment
questions.explain: Euthanasia refers to deliberately ending a life, usually to relieve incurable suffering.

questions.q: Which view best describes a liberal Christian attitude to remarriage after divorce?
options: Marriage is never a serious commitment
Remarriage may be permitted as God offers forgiveness and new beginnings
Divorced people must leave the faith
Remarriage is forbidden in all circumstances
questions.explain: Some Christians believe forgiveness and compassion allow for remarriage after divorce.

questions.q: Which religious group is well known for clergy taking vows of celibacy?
options: All Muslim imams
All Jewish rabbis
Roman Catholic priests
All Protestant ministers
questions.explain: Roman Catholic priests typically take vows of celibacy, unlike clergy in many other traditions who may marry.

questions.q: Why might some religious believers oppose certain fertility treatments?
options: Because they replace the need for families
Because they may involve discarding unused embryos, raising sanctity-of-life concerns
Because they are illegal
Because they always fail
questions.explain: Some object where embryos are destroyed, viewing this as conflicting with the sanctity of life.

questions.q: Which view best reflects a 'pro-life' position on abortion?
options: That the foetus is not alive at any stage
That the unborn child has a right to life from conception
That life only begins at adulthood
That abortion is always the woman's free choice
questions.explain: The pro-life position holds that human life begins at conception and should be protected.

questions.q: According to traditional Christian teaching, what is one of the main purposes of marriage?
options: To guarantee a couple will never face difficulty
To gain financial advantage over others
To provide a stable, loving union for procreation and mutual support
To remove the need for religious commitment
questions.explain: Many Christian traditions teach that marriage is for lifelong companionship, mutual support and the raising of children.

questions.q: Which of these is a reason a believer might give for opposing pollution and waste?
options: The Earth belongs only to humans to exploit
Future generations do not matter
Pollution improves creation
Damaging the planet fails in the God-given duty of stewardship
questions.explain: Believers often argue that polluting the Earth neglects the responsibility to care for God's creation.

questions.q: What is 'cohabitation'?
options: A vow of lifelong celibacy
A form of religious pilgrimage
Living together as a couple without being married
A religious ceremony of marriage
questions.explain: Cohabitation means a couple living together in a sexual relationship without being legally married.

questions.q: What is one religious argument sometimes given in support of traditional gender roles in the family?
options: That such roles are based on certain scriptural teachings about complementary responsibilities
That women are not human
That children should raise themselves
That men should not work
questions.explain: Some believers cite scripture to support distinct but complementary roles, though others interpret these texts differently.
